# Foundation gap report

<!-- Generated by hack/coverage/run.sh from the coverage data, hack/coverage/foundation.yaml (the research) and hack/coverage/module-usage.csv; do not edit. -->

The ranked work queue for the kind agents. It covers every resource in the two categories a platform team needs first, *platform-foundation* (Organizations and Control Tower, IAM and Identity Center, VPC networking and DNS, KMS, CloudTrail, RAM, EKS and ECR) and *security-adjacent* (Config, GuardDuty, Security Hub, WAF, Secrets Manager, ACM and the like), as the builder defined them on 2026-11-09. Application primitives (S3, SQS, Lambda, RDS, ...) are not here; the [coverage README](../../README.md#coverage) shows them.

**How to use it.** Take the first item in the [work queue](#work-queue) that is not built; [docs/handoff.md](../handoff.md) says how a gap kind is built and checked here. Each item names the kinds to build, what upstream already has (so you copy before you write, `CONTRIBUTING.md`), whether moto can prove it, and when it is done. The [every-resource tables](#every-resource-ranked) are the same ranking at resource level, with the numbers regenerated from `config/crds/` on each run, so an item that gets built moves down by itself.

### F01 AWS Organizations: SCPs and the other policy types, attachment, delegated administrators, organization features, account placement

- **Resources:** `organizations/Policy`, `organizations/Organization`, `organizations/Account`, `organizations/ResourcePolicy`. Today ACK covers 5, ours 8, nothing covers 4 of 17 attributes.
- **Why first:** The builder's first ask: manage accounts, OUs and SCPs early and show it to platform teams. ACK ships `Account` and `OrganizationalUnit` but ignores `Policy` and `Organization`, so there is no way to declare an SCP, attach it, delegate an administrator or enable a policy type. Three of the five Organizations resources in CloudFormation are open here, and the API has more (delegated administrators, service access and policy-type enablement have no CloudFormation resource, so they are in none of the coverage numbers).
- **Proposed kinds:** In `organizations.aws.hfl.dev`, beside ACK's `Account` and `OrganizationalUnit`:
  - (1) `Policy`: generated from `CreatePolicy`/`DescribePolicy`/`UpdatePolicy`/`DeletePolicy`; `name`, `description`, `type` (immutable: `SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY`, `TAG_POLICY`, `BACKUP_POLICY`, `AISERVICES_OPT_OUT_POLICY` and the newer types), `content` (a JSON document, compared as canonical JSON), `tags`.
  - (2) `PolicyAttachment`: hand-written on the `RolePolicyAttachment` skeleton (iam-controller PR #184): `policyID` or `policyRef`, `targetID` or `targetRef` (ACK's `OrganizationalUnit` or `Account`, or the root), `AttachPolicy`/`DetachPolicy`, read with `ListPoliciesForTarget`; non-exclusive (it never detaches policies it did not attach), the precedent being `Role.policies` against `RolePolicyAttachment`. CloudFormation's `Policy.TargetIds` is the exclusive form: do not add it to `Policy`.
  - (3) `DelegatedAdministrator`: hand-written, `accountID` or `accountRef` and `servicePrincipal`; `RegisterDelegatedAdministrator`/`DeregisterDelegatedAdministrator`, read with `ListDelegatedAdministrators`.
  - (4) `Organization`: hand-written singleton on the shape of our `ReplicationConfiguration`: `featureSet`, `enabledPolicyTypes[]` (`EnablePolicyType`/`DisablePolicyType` on the root), `awsServiceAccessPrincipals[]` (`EnableAWSServiceAccess`/`DisableAWSServiceAccess`); adopts the existing organization, creating one only if told to.
  - (5) `AccountPlacement`: hand-written sidecar by `accountRef`/`accountID` and `parentID`/`parentRef`: `MoveAccount`, read with `ListParents` (community #2369).
- **Upstream:** ACK `organizations-controller` v1.7.0 has `Account` and `OrganizationalUnit`; its `generator.yaml` ignores `Policy`, `Organization` and `GovCloudAccount`. Community #2884 (2026-05-11) proposes `Policy`, `PolicyAttachment` and `DelegatedAdministrator` in three PRs and the reporter offers to write them; no pull request is open at 2026-11-09. The rule in `CLAUDE.md` and plan section 3: build here when upstream has neither released nor a PR close to merging; that is the case today. Recheck #2884 before starting each kind and re-copy if a PR appears.
- **moto (5.2.5):** Good: `CreateOrganization`, `CreateAccount`, `CreateOrganizationalUnit`, `CreatePolicy`/`UpdatePolicy`/`DeletePolicy`, `AttachPolicy`/`DetachPolicy`, `EnablePolicyType`, `EnableAWSServiceAccess`, `RegisterDelegatedAdministrator`/`DeregisterDelegatedAdministrator`, `MoveAccount`, `ListPoliciesForTarget`, `ListRoots`, `TagResource` are implemented, so kinds (1) to (5) can be proved end to end. Not implemented: `PutResourcePolicy` (so `ResourcePolicy` cannot be proved), `DescribeEffectivePolicy`, `EnableAllFeatures`, `InviteAccountToOrganization`.
- **Modules:** None of the 40 tracked terraform-aws-modules creates an Organizations resource (Terraform users use `aws_organizations_*` directly, or a landing-zone module outside the tracked set); a module need of 0 here is a gap in the module space, not low demand.
- **Size:** M (Policy), M (PolicyAttachment), S (DelegatedAdministrator), M (Organization), S (AccountPlacement); plus one for the new `services/organizations/` manager
- **Approach:** Start with `Policy`: create `services/organizations/` like `services/rds/`: a `generator.yaml` that ignores `Account` and `OrganizationalUnit` (ACK has them) and configures `Policy` (start from the shape of ACK's `OrganizationalUnit` entry at organizations-controller commit `5824700fd7`), generate with `hack/generate.sh`, add the manager to the operator's mapping and `config/rbac`. The SDK client is `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/organizations`; pin it to the version ACK's `organizations-controller` v1.7.0 `go.mod` names, as `UPSTREAM.md` does for the others. Then `PolicyAttachment` and `DelegatedAdministrator` by copying `services/iam/pkg/resource/role_policy_attachment/`, and `Organization` from `services/ecr/pkg/resource/replication_configuration/`.
  - An SCP document is JSON: reuse the canonical-JSON comparison of `services/lambda/pkg/resource/permission/` (it reads policy statements) so key order and whitespace do not cause a delta. Test only what moto implements and write the rest in `docs/plan.md`, as the fake cloud's doc requires.
- **Done when:** Each kind has an end-to-end test in `tests/e2e` on moto (create, update or refusal, delete, `deletion-policy: retain`); `task check` passes; the README table and `docs/plan.md` list the kinds; `task coverage` shows `organizations/Policy` at 100% and moves the `organizations` bar; `PolicyAttachment` attaches a policy to an ACK-made `OrganizationalUnit` by `targetRef` in one apply.

### F02 IAM Identity Center: permission sets and account assignments

- **Resources:** `sso/PermissionSet`, `sso/Assignment`, `sso/Instance`, `sso/InstanceAccessControlAttributeConfiguration`. Today ACK covers 0, ours 25, nothing covers 3 of 28 attributes.
- **Why first:** How people get into accounts: a platform team's access model is permission sets assigned to groups per account. ACK has no controller (the `ssoadmin-controller` repository is empty), no PR, only an open request since 2023. It is the other half of the builder's account story.
- **Proposed kinds:** In `ssoadmin.aws.hfl.dev` (ACK's service id is `ssoadmin`, so the group will match when ACK ships one; CloudFormation calls the service `sso`):
  - (1) `PermissionSet`: `name`, `description`, `sessionDuration`, `relayState`, `tags`, `managedPolicies[]` (ARNs), `customerManagedPolicyReferences[]` (name and path), `inlinePolicy` (JSON), `permissionsBoundary`; `instanceARN` or the organization's only instance found with `ListInstances`. Generated base from `CreatePermissionSet`/`DescribePermissionSet`/`UpdatePermissionSet`/`DeletePermissionSet`, with hooks for the attachment APIs (`AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet`, `AttachCustomerManagedPolicyReferenceToPermissionSet`, `PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet`, `PutPermissionsBoundaryToPermissionSet`) and `ProvisionPermissionSet` after a change that reaches assigned accounts.
  - (2) `Assignment`: hand-written on the `RolePolicyAttachment` skeleton: `permissionSetRef`/`permissionSetARN`, `principalType` (`USER` or `GROUP`), `principalID`, `targetAccountID` or `targetAccountRef` (ACK's organizations `Account`); `CreateAccountAssignment`/`DeleteAccountAssignment` are asynchronous, so synced waits on `DescribeAccountAssignmentCreationStatus`; read with `ListAccountAssignments`.
  - (3) `InstanceAccessControlAttributeConfiguration`: hand-written singleton, low priority (attribute-based access control).
  - `Instance` is not a kind: an organization has one instance, found by `ListInstances` (creating one is a console act or `CreateInstance`); take `instanceARN` as a field.
- **Upstream:** No controller release: `ssoadmin-controller` holds only the 2023-07-27 initial commit. Community #1857 (open, three reactions). No pull request. Nothing to copy but ACK's conventions.
- **moto (5.2.5):** Mostly good: `CreatePermissionSet`/`DescribePermissionSet`/`UpdatePermissionSet`, `AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet`, `AttachCustomerManagedPolicyReferenceToPermissionSet`, `PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet`, `CreateAccountAssignment`/`DeleteAccountAssignment`/`ListAccountAssignments`/`DescribeAccountAssignmentCreationStatus`, `ProvisionPermissionSet`, `ListInstances`. Not implemented: `PutPermissionsBoundaryToPermissionSet` and `CreateInstanceAccessControlAttributeConfiguration`: those two cannot be proved.
- **Modules:** 0 of 40: no terraform-aws-modules module wraps Identity Center (the Terraform resources are `aws_ssoadmin_*`).
- **Size:** L (PermissionSet: six APIs behind one kind), M (Assignment: async), S (attribute config); plus one for the new `services/ssoadmin/` manager
- **Approach:** Copy conventions from `services/iam/`. `PermissionSet` is the hard one: ACK's code generator makes the base kind from the Create/Describe pair, but policy attachment is a set of separate calls, so write the diff of `managedPolicies[]` and `customerManagedPolicyReferences[]` as an update hook (`ListManagedPoliciesInPermissionSet`, `ListCustomerManagedPolicyReferencesInPermissionSet`, `GetInlinePolicyForPermissionSet`); ram-controller's `ResourceShare` update hook (`templates/hooks/resource_share/sdk_update_pre_build_request.go.tpl`) is a worked example of syncing a list through separate calls. Call `ProvisionPermissionSet` only after an update, and report not-synced until its request status is `SUCCEEDED`.
  - Do not write `identitystore` here: users and groups are item F12.
- **Done when:** `PermissionSet` and `Assignment` pass end-to-end tests on moto (create, update a policy list and see `ProvisionPermissionSet` called, delete, retain); the two moto-less calls are listed in `docs/plan.md` as untested; a chart can create a permission set and assign it to an ACK `Account` by reference; `task check` passes; `task coverage` shows `sso` above 0%.

### F03 IAM: SAML providers (and the access-key question)

- **Resources:** `iam/SAMLProvider`, `iam/AccessKey`, `iam/VirtualMFADevice`, `iam/ServerCertificate`, `iam/OIDCProvider`, `iam/ManagedPolicy`. Today ACK covers 9, ours 12, nothing covers 15 of 36 attributes.
- **Why first:** Federation into the account is what a platform team wires first after roles and policies: `OpenIDConnectProvider` is covered (EKS IRSA), `SAMLProvider` is not and ACK ignores it. The rest of IAM that a platform team uses (roles, policies, boundaries through `Role.permissionsBoundary`, instance profiles, service-linked roles, users, groups, OIDC) is covered by ACK; ours already adds `RolePolicyAttachment`, `UserGroupMembership`, `LoginProfile`, `SSHPublicKey`, `AccountAlias` and `AccountPasswordPolicy`.
- **Proposed kinds:** `iam.aws.hfl.dev/SAMLProvider`, generated: `CreateSAMLProvider`, `GetSAMLProvider`, `UpdateSAMLProvider`, `DeleteSAMLProvider`; `name` (immutable), `samlMetadataDocument` (the XML, read from a Secret or inline), `assertionEncryptionMode`, `addPrivateKey`/`removePrivateKey`, `tags`. The ARN is the identifier.
  - `AccessKey`: recommend NOT building. The secret is returned once on create; a kind needs a Kubernetes Secret write-back and the key is a long-lived credential (community #1879 asks for it). If the builder wants it, hand-write it on the `LoginProfile` pattern (which already writes a password) and add the Secret write-back in the same change.
  - `VirtualMFADevice` and `ServerCertificate`: low priority (a person's device; a legacy resource).
- **Upstream:** ACK `iam-controller` v1.11.3 ignores `SAMLProvider`, `AccessKey`, `VirtualMFADevice`, `ServiceSpecificCredential`, `PolicyVersion`, `LoginProfile`, `AccountAlias`. No PR for `SAMLProvider`. PR #167 (group membership, open) and #184 (`RolePolicyAttachment`, open) are already tracked in `UPSTREAM.md`.
- **moto (5.2.5):** Good: `CreateSAMLProvider`, `CreateAccessKey`, `CreateVirtualMFADevice` are implemented.
- **Modules:** `iam` (#1, ranked first by downloads): `iam-user` (access key, login profile, SSH key), `iam-account` (alias, password policy; both ours already). SAML providers are in no tracked module.
- **Size:** S (SAMLProvider), M (AccessKey if wanted)
- **Approach:** Add `SAMLProvider` to the generated-kind setup of `services/iam/` (`generator.yaml`, which already ignores what ACK has). The SAML metadata is a document: take it from `samlMetadataSecretRef` so it is not in the spec.
- **Done when:** `SAMLProvider` passes an end-to-end test on moto (create, update metadata, delete, retain); README and `docs/plan.md` updated; `task coverage` moves `iam/SAMLProvider` to 100%.

### F04 EC2 networking: Transit Gateway route tables, associations, propagation, routes and peering

- **Resources:** `ec2/TransitGatewayRouteTable`, `ec2/TransitGatewayRouteTableAssociation`, `ec2/TransitGatewayRouteTablePropagation`, `ec2/TransitGatewayRoute`, `ec2/TransitGatewayPeeringAttachment`, `ec2/TransitGateway`, `ec2/TransitGatewayVpcAttachment`. Today ACK covers 20, ours 17, nothing covers 6 of 43 attributes.
- **Why first:** A Transit Gateway is how a platform team joins VPCs and accounts. ACK has `TransitGateway` and the VPC attachment only; without route tables a gateway routes everything through its default table. Its generator also ignores `ModifyTransitGateway`, so a gateway's options cannot change after create.
- **Proposed kinds:** In `ec2.aws.hfl.dev`: `TransitGatewayRouteTable`, generated from `CreateTransitGatewayRouteTable`/`DescribeTransitGatewayRouteTables`/`DeleteTransitGatewayRouteTable`, with `associations[]` (attachment refs, `AssociateTransitGatewayRouteTable`), `propagations[]` (`EnableTransitGatewayRouteTablePropagation`) and `routes[]` (`CreateTransitGatewayRoute`, static or blackhole) as fields, the way ACK's `RouteTable` carries routes (see its route handling in ec2-controller `pkg/resource/route_table/hooks.go`). `TransitGatewayPeeringAttachment`, generated, with the peer account's accept step as a field.
  - Then ask ACK for `ModifyTransitGateway`: four `TransitGateway` attributes are uncovered (`AssociationDefaultRouteTableId` and `PropagationDefaultRouteTableId`, which only make sense once route tables are kinds, `EncryptionSupport` and `SecurityGroupReferencingSupport`).
- **Upstream:** `ec2-controller` v1.23.1 ignores `TransitGatewayRouteTable`, `TransitGatewayRoute`, `TransitGatewayPeeringAttachment`, `TransitGatewayConnect`, `TransitGatewayConnectPeer` and the operation `ModifyTransitGateway`. No open PR or issue for them (#1865 `TransitGatewayAttachment` is closed). Recheck before starting.
- **moto (5.2.5):** Good: `CreateTransitGateway`, `CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment`, `CreateTransitGatewayRouteTable`, `AssociateTransitGatewayRouteTable`, `EnableTransitGatewayRouteTablePropagation`, `CreateTransitGatewayRoute` and `CreateTransitGatewayPeeringAttachment` are implemented.
- **Modules:** `transit-gateway` (#32): gateway, route tables, VPC attachments, routes, RAM share; `vpn-gateway` (#30) attaches to a gateway; `vpc` (#3) can attach to one.
- **Size:** M, M
- **Approach:** Add the kinds to `services/ec2/` (it has the EC2 SDK client at ACK's version and our patch 0002). Start from the generator entries and hook templates of ACK's `TransitGateway` and `RouteTable` at ec2-controller `9303654c`; record each copied file in `UPSTREAM.md`. `transitGatewayRef` and `attachmentRef` should resolve to ACK's `TransitGateway` and `TransitGatewayVPCAttachment`; plan section 8, point 10 describes the limit on kinds that reference ACK's own kinds of the same service (the generator rewrites ACK's import path): read it first.
- **Done when:** End-to-end tests on moto for a gateway with two VPC attachments, a route table, an association, a propagation and a blackhole route, then deletion in dependency order; `task check`; `task coverage` moves `ec2/TransitGatewayRouteTable` to 100%.

### F05 EC2 networking: site-to-site VPN connections and route propagation

- **Resources:** `ec2/VPNConnection`, `ec2/VPNConnectionRoute`, `ec2/VPNGatewayRoutePropagation`, `ec2/VPNGateway`, `ec2/CustomerGateway`. Today ACK covers 0, ours 50, nothing covers 9 of 59 attributes.
- **Why first:** Hybrid connectivity: a customer gateway and a VPN gateway (ours already) mean nothing without the connection that joins them. ACK has none of the three; community #1868 has asked since 2023.
- **Proposed kinds:** `ec2.aws.hfl.dev/VPNConnection`, generated from `CreateVpnConnection`/`DescribeVpnConnections`/`DeleteVpnConnection`: `type`, `customerGatewayRef` and `vpnGatewayRef` (our kinds) or `transitGatewayRef` (ACK's), `staticRoutesOnly`, `tunnelOptions[]` (two tunnels: pre-shared key from a Secret, CIDRs, IKE and phase lifetimes), `staticRoutes[]` (a field, `CreateVpnConnectionRoute`), tags. 43 CloudFormation attributes: the largest EC2 networking kind. Route propagation to a route table is a field of `RouteTable` upstream (`EnableVgwRoutePropagation`) or a small sidecar kind of ours.
- **Upstream:** ec2-controller ignores `VpnConnection`, `VpnConnectionRoute`, `VpnGateway`, `CustomerGateway` in generator.yaml. Community #1868 'VPN resources' (open since 2023-08-03, ten comments, no PR). Ours: `VPNGateway`, `CustomerGateway`.
- **moto (5.2.5):** Partial: `CreateVpnConnection`, `CreateVpnGateway`, `AttachVpnGateway`, `CreateCustomerGateway` are implemented; `CreateVpnConnectionRoute` and `EnableVgwRoutePropagation` are not, so static routes and propagation cannot be proved on moto.
- **Modules:** `vpn-gateway` (#30) and `vpc` (#3).
- **Size:** L (VPNConnection), S (propagation)
- **Approach:** Add to `services/ec2/` next to `vpn_gateway` and `customer_gateway`, whose hooks and references you copy (`hooks.go`, `templates/hooks/vpn_gateway/`). The tunnel pre-shared keys are secrets: take them from a `secretKeyRef` as ACK's kinds do. Write what moto cannot show in the fake cloud's section of `docs/plan.md`.
- **Done when:** An end-to-end test creates a connection from our `CustomerGateway` and `VPNGateway`, updates a tunnel option and deletes it; static routes and propagation are documented as unproved; `task coverage` moves `ec2/VPNConnection` above 90%.

### F07 Control Tower: landing zone, enabled controls, enabled baselines

- **Resources:** `controltower/LandingZone`, `controltower/EnabledControl`, `controltower/EnabledBaseline`. Today ACK covers 0, ours 13, nothing covers 5 of 18 attributes.
- **Why first:** Where a platform team runs a multi-account landing zone, Control Tower is how guardrails are enabled. The builder asked for it 'where it has APIs': it has three CloudFormation resources and an asynchronous API. It ranks here, not first, because nothing can prove it yet.
- **Proposed kinds:** In a new service `controltower.aws.hfl.dev`: `EnabledControl` (`EnableControl`/`GetEnabledControl`/`DisableControl`; the target is an OU ARN, with a control identifier and parameters), `EnabledBaseline` (`EnableBaseline`/`GetEnabledBaseline`/`DisableBaseline`), `LandingZone` (`CreateLandingZone`/`GetLandingZone`/`UpdateLandingZone`/`DeleteLandingZone`; the manifest is a JSON document, plus a version). All three are asynchronous: each call returns an operation identifier to poll (`GetControlOperation`, `GetBaselineOperation`, `GetLandingZoneOperation`), so write them by hand on the `Assignment` skeleton of F02 with a status poll rather than generating them.
- **Upstream:** No ACK repository, issue or pull request found. Nothing to copy.
- **moto (5.2.5):** None: moto 5.2.5 has no `controltower`. **Blocked**: the repository's rule is to prove kinds only against recordings or emulators named in `docs/plan.md`; none exists for this API. Either record the calls from a real account (not allowed here) or write a small test double for the harness; that is the builder's call (open question for plan section 9).

- **Size:** L each, and no emulator
- **Approach:** Do after F01 and F02, because `EnabledControl` targets an OU that ACK's `OrganizationalUnit` creates. If the builder approves a test double, keep it in `pkg/test/` as a small HTTP fake of the three operation pairs, with the polling states the real service returns.

### F10 CloudTrail: start logging and select events on a Trail (and organization trails)

- **Resources:** `cloudtrail/Trail`, `cloudtrail/EventDataStore`, `cloudtrail/ResourcePolicy`, `cloudtrail/Channel`, `cloudtrail/Dashboard`. Today ACK covers 28, ours 0, nothing covers 47 of 75 attributes.

ACK's `Trail` covers 13 of 31 attributes including `isOrganizationTrail`, `isMultiRegionTrail`, the bucket, KMS key and log file validation, but a Trail it creates is never told to `StartLogging` (no `isLogging` field, and the controller's hooks make no such call) and has no event, advanced event or insight selectors. An organization trail is only useful once it logs.
- **Proposed kinds:** A sidecar kind `cloudtrail.aws.hfl.dev/TrailLogging` that references an ACK `Trail` by `trailRef` or `trailARN`: `isLogging`, `eventSelectors[]`, `advancedEventSelectors[]`, `insightSelectors[]`, calling `StartLogging`/`StopLogging`, `PutEventSelectors`, `PutAdvancedEventSelectors`, `PutInsightSelectors`. Hand-written on the `RolePolicyAttachment` skeleton. The alternative is to add the fields to ACK's `Trail` upstream (plan section 9, question 1: wait for the release unless a package cannot work without the field; a trail that does not log cannot work, so this meets the rule). `ResourcePolicy`, `Channel`, `Dashboard`: low priority.

- **moto (5.2.5):** Good for the first three: `StartLogging`, `StopLogging`, `PutEventSelectors`, `GetEventSelectors`, `PutInsightSelectors`, `GetTrailStatus` are implemented. `PutAdvancedEventSelectors` is not in moto's coverage list, and event data stores and channels are not implemented.
- **Modules:** None of the 40 tracked modules creates a Trail.
- **Size:** M
- **Approach:** New `services/cloudtrail/` manager (there is none yet). Read ACK's `Trail` hook (`pkg/resource/trail/hooks.go` at cloudtrail-controller v1.9.1) to see its tag and update handling before you write.
- **Done when:** An end-to-end test creates an ACK `Trail` and a `TrailLogging` that starts logging with one event selector, flips `isLogging` off and on, and deletes; the advanced-selector call is documented as unproved; `task coverage` moves `cloudtrail/Trail` above 70%.

## Every resource, ranked

One section per service in queue order; inside a service, resources that still need something first, then by modules that need them, then by size. Columns:

- **ACK**: the released kind and how many of the resource's attributes it covers; **Ours**: our kinds and the attributes they add beyond ACK.
- **Missing**: `whole resource`, or the attributes nothing covers (required ones and shallow ones first, unless `foundation.yaml` names the ones that matter); `covered inline` means ACK (or ours) covers it as fields of another kind, so the number is not a gap in practice (the coverage CSVs do not credit it).
- **Modules**: how many of the 40 tracked terraform-aws-modules create it (their Terraform resource types, paired by name and by [`mappings.yaml`](../../hack/coverage/mappings.yaml) `terraform:`); 0 is not 'unneeded' for services no public module wraps.
- **moto**: whether moto 5.2.5, our only emulator, implements the API; **Size**: from `foundation.yaml`, else estimated from the attribute count (S up to 15, M up to 60, L above); **Item**: the queue item that builds it.

### platform-foundation: `ec2`

- **ACK controller:** `ec2-controller` v1.23.1: 20 kinds (VPC, Subnet, RouteTable, InternetGateway, EgressOnlyInternetGateway, NATGateway, ElasticIPAddress, NetworkACL, SecurityGroup, ManagedPrefixList, DHCPOptions, VPCEndpoint, VPCEndpointServiceConfiguration, VPCPeeringConnection, TransitGateway, TransitGatewayVPCAttachment, FlowLog, Instance, LaunchTemplate, CapacityReservation); routes, ACL entries, security group rules and subnet associations are fields of those kinds, not kinds
- **Ignored in ACK's `generator.yaml`:** `CustomerGateway`, `VpnGateway`, `VpnConnection`, `VpnConnectionRoute`, `TransitGatewayRouteTable`, `TransitGatewayRoute`, `TransitGatewayPeeringAttachment`, `TransitGatewayConnect`, `TransitGatewayConnectPeer`, `TransitGatewayPolicyTable`, `TransitGatewayPrefixListReference`, `TransitGatewayMulticastDomain`, `Route`, `NetworkAclEntry`, `NetworkInterface`, `NetworkInterfacePermission`, `PlacementGroup`, `KeyPair`, `VpcCidrBlock`, `VpcBlockPublicAccessExclusion`, `VpcEncryptionControl`, `SubnetCidrReservation`, `VpcEndpointConnectionNotification`, `Ipam`, `IpamPool`, `IpamScope`, `ClientVpnEndpoint`, `Volume`, `Snapshot`, `Fleet`
- **Upstream:** Open PRs: #396 `KeyPair`, #308 `Fleet`; the rest are fixes (#394 and #385 security group rules, #383, #377, #376, #404). `generator.yaml` also ignores the operations `ModifyTransitGateway` and `ModifyVpcEndpoint`, so a Transit Gateway's options and an endpoint's settings cannot be changed after create. Community #1868 'VPN resources' (open since 2023-08-03, ten comments), #1865 `TransitGatewayAttachment` (closed).
- **moto:** moto `ec2`: 232 of 809 operations. Implemented: Transit Gateway, its VPC and peering attachments, route tables, association, propagation and routes; `CreateVpnConnection`, `CreateVpnGateway`, `AttachVpnGateway`, `CreateCustomerGateway`; `CreateNetworkInterface`; flow logs; endpoints and endpoint services; managed prefix lists; peering; `CreateTags`. Not implemented: `CreateVpnConnectionRoute`, `EnableVgwRoutePropagation`, `CreatePlacementGroup`, `CreateVpcBlockPublicAccessExclusion`, `ModifyVpcBlockPublicAccessOptions`.

## Sources and pins

Researched 2026-11-09, read-only.

- ACK controllers: the latest release of each, pinned in [sources.yaml](sources.yaml); `generator.yaml` of each read at its release commit (raw.githubusercontent.com, read-only). A resource in a generator's `ignore.resource_names` is ignored on purpose or not yet wired.
- ACK open pull requests of the controllers named below: `gh pr list --repo aws-controllers-k8s/<service>-controller --state open`, 2026-11-09.
- ACK `community` issues: `gh search issues` and `gh api repos/aws-controllers-k8s/community/issues/<n>`, 2026-11-09 (numbers are cited where they are used).
- moto 5.2.5 (the version `hack/moto-requirements.txt` pins): `IMPLEMENTATION_COVERAGE.md` at tag 5.2.5, which marks each API operation as implemented or not. 'Implemented' means a handler exists, not that every field behaves as AWS does.
- Module need: [`module-usage.csv`](../../hack/coverage/module-usage.csv), the AWS rows of the High Five Labs catalog's `docs/coverage/resource-types.csv` at catalog commit `debccf7362c21a2f633f24ee92f51852213994af` (40 terraform-aws-modules at the releases pinned in the catalog's `upstream/modules.yaml`, 469 resource-type uses), and the gap ranking in the catalog's `docs/aws.md` (commit `b6fdd5342346997fe855357eeee225afb7530e95`, sha256 `8c2ab34d8e50130e19bfa0619ffc0c9800646d26e8bebac9de347a574a681533`).
- Which of our kinds exist: `config/crds/bases/` of this commit; which are copied from open PRs: `UPSTREAM.md`.
